rows.note: This is the all-purpose verb for pouring a liquid out of or into a container.

example.english: I’ll pour you a glass of water.
example.jyutping: ngo5 bong1 nei5 dou2 bui1 seoi2

rows.note: Use this specifically when rain is falling heavily and continuously.

example.english: It’s going to pour heavily, so don’t go out now.
example.traditional: 而家落大雨，唔好出街喇。
example.jyutping: ji4 gaa1 lok6 daai6 jyu5 m4 hou2 ceot1 gaai1 laa3

rows.note: Use this for pouring out or venting emotions, anger, or abuse rather than for liquid.

example.english: Don’t pour your anger out on me.
example.jyutping: nei5 m4 hou2 lo2 ngo5 lei4 faat3 sit3 wo3

rows.note: Use this when a crowd streams or surges along, usually with a directional complement such as 出嚟 or 入去.

example.english: During rush hour, crowds pour into the MTR station.
example.traditional: 放工時間，人潮湧入去地鐵站。
example.jyutping: fong3 gung1 si4 gaan3 jan4 ciu4 jung2 jap6 heoi3 dei6 tit3 zaam6
